input.quote: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: Section 12.4 binds Customer with a non-compete that runs for the term plus twenty-four months post-term, covers "any product or service that competes with Vendor" in "any territory", and even bars acquisitions. That is walk-away territory under this rule: the post-term tail exceeds 12 months, the scope is undefined, and there is no named product, term-only limit, or carve-out for internal development or acquisitions, so it fails every fallback element. It also directly contradicts Section 12.3, which records that Customer has made no non-compete commitment. We therefore take the preferred position and remove the restriction from Section 12.4 with the shortest conforming edit, leaving Section 12.3 intact.

ops.oldText: During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
ops.newText: Customer is not restricted from developing, marketing, selling, or acquiring any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot restrict the products or services we develop, market, sell, or acquire, so we have replaced the 24-month all-territory non-compete in Section 12.4 with a confirmation that no such restriction applies (consistent with Section 12.3). If you need protection, we could discuss a restriction limited to one named competing product during the term only, with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.
proposal.summary: Remove the 24-month all-territory non-compete on Customer in Section 12.4.

mappings.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.
